info.title: Topup.dev API
info.description:
Place and track digital game top-up / gift-card fulfilment orders.

**Authentication** — send your API key as a Bearer token:
`Authorization: Bearer tg_live_…`. Keys come in two environments:
- `tg_live_…` — real orders (debits your prepaid balance, dispatches to the engine).
- `tg_test_…` — **sandbox**: orders are simulated (no balance, no engine, no real delivery), so you can build your integration end-to-end for free. To simulate a *failed* order in the sandbox, set `player.uid` to `"fail"`.

**Idempotency** — every order create must send an `Idempotency-Key` header that is **unique to that order**. Generate a fresh one per order (a UUID, or your own order id); a hardcoded or reused key returns the FIRST order again and creates nothing, which looks exactly like success. Test and live never share keys — reusing one across environments is rejected with 409.

**Webhooks** — configure endpoints in your dashboard to receive `order.fulfilled` / `order.failed` / `order.refunded` events. For flexible-priced products (e.g. Razer Payment) also subscribe to `order.awaiting_confirmation`, which fires when the upstream price needs your OK (act via POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/confirm | /decline). Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`tg-signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`); the signed string is `${t}.${rawBody}`. Sandbox orders deliver too, with `livemode: false`.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: Discover services and their products + prices.

get.description: Your orders, newest first. Cursor-paginated: pass the previous response's `next_cursor` as `?cursor=`. A live key lists live orders; a test key lists sandbox orders.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: Only the orders of one bulk batch (see POST /api/v1/orders/batch).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An order id from a prior `next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `?cursor=` for the next page; null when no more.

post.description:
Creates a fulfilment order for a catalog SKU. Requires an `ingest` or `admin` key and a unique `Idempotency-Key` header. With a `tg_test_` key the order is simulated.

**This is not a price quote.** The response is the created order, which usually starts `queued`. For **flexible-priced products (e.g. Razer Payment)** the price is not known at create time — the engine learns it from the upstream a moment later and writes it to `confirmed_price_cents` (NOT `amount_cents`, which is the cost basis and is `0` for payment-link / BYO products). Get the final price by polling `GET /api/v1/orders/{id}` until `confirmed_price_cents` is set (or the order reaches `fulfilled`), or from the `order.fulfilled` webhook, which now carries `confirmed_price_cents`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A **new, unique value for every order** — generate one per order (a UUID, or your own order id), never a constant and never a counter you might restart. Sending the same key twice returns the FIRST order again (200) and creates nothing, so a hardcoded key silently stops placing orders. Keys are also never shared between `tg_test_` and `tg_live_`: a key already used in the other environment is rejected with 409.

razer_payment.summary: Razer Payment (payment-link product) — flexible price, no uid

200.description: Idempotent replay — this Idempotency-Key was already used, so this is the ORIGINAL order and nothing was created. If you did not intend a retry, your key generation is buggy: treat an unexpected 200 as an error, not a success.

402.description: insufficient_balance · subscription_past_due — top up to proceed.

409.description: idempotency_key_environment_mismatch — this Idempotency-Key was already used by a key from the other environment (test vs live). Test and live never share keys. Send a new unique key, and clear any sandbox keys out of your live data.

post.description: Creates up to 100 orders of one SKU in a single call. Each item becomes a fully independent order (own id, own balance hold, fulfilled one-by-one) — the batch groups them for display and code export. Creation is all-or-nothing: an underfunded or invalid batch creates nothing. The `Idempotency-Key` header applies to the whole batch; a batch of N consumes N rate-limit slots. With a `tg_test_` key the batch is simulated (`player.uid="fail"` fails that one item).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A **new, unique value for every batch** — generate one per batch, never a constant. Sending the same key twice returns the FIRST batch again (200) and creates nothing. Keys are never shared between `tg_test_` and `tg_live_`; reusing one across environments is rejected with 409.

voucher_codes.summary: Redeem codes of one product (repeat the empty item N times)

same_player_many_times.summary: Many top-ups for ONE player — repeat the same item N times

200.description: Idempotent replay — this Idempotency-Key was already used, so this is the ORIGINAL batch and nothing was created. An unexpected 200 means your key generation is buggy.

201.description: Batch created — every item is queued.

409.description: idempotency_key_environment_mismatch — this Idempotency-Key was already used by a key from the other environment (test vs live). Send a new unique key.

get.description: The batch with all of its orders and a rolled-up `status`: `queued`, `processing`, `awaiting_confirmation`, `partial` (some fulfilled, some failed), `fulfilled`, or `failed`.

File download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). `txt` = one code per line, only items that delivered a code. `csv` = every item with columns `order_id,position,sku,product,status,code,created_at` (empty code for unfulfilled items, so the file reconciles against `item_count`).

post.description: For flexible-priced products the order may pause in `awaiting_confirmation` with a `confirmed_price_cents`. Confirm to proceed (charges the confirmed price).
Rejects the confirmed price; the order fails and any hold is refunded.

get.description: Platform services (bundles + batch flows) available to this workspace. `enabled` is whether the workspace opted in. Each service lists its products with prices (bundle members, or the single target product for batch flows).
The workspace prepaid balance. Orders are charged against it; a `direct`/managed order needs `price_cents` available or it fails with `insufficient_balance`.

The workspace ledger, newest first — deposits, order charges, refunds, subscription fees. Each entry is a signed `delta_cents` with the running `balance_after_cents`. Cursor-paginated via `next_cursor`.

post.description: Requires an `admin` key. The response includes the signing `secret` ONCE — store it to verify the `tg-signature` header (`t=<ts>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<ts>.<body>")>`).

patch.description: Admin key. Partial update of `url` / `events` / `status` (the secret is not changed).

post.description: Admin key. Returns a new `secret` ONCE; the old secret stops validating immediately.

bearerAuth.description: API key as a Bearer token: `tg_live_…` (live) or `tg_test_…` (sandbox).

Player.description: Recipient/target. For most products provide `uid` (or `email`). **Payment-link products (e.g. Razer Payment)** take a `PaymentLink` instead — that URL is the order target, so `uid` is not required for them. A method may declare extra required fields (see `required_fields` on the catalog delivery option, e.g. `ServerId`); send each as a same-named key here and it is forwarded to the upstream as-is.

uid.description: Game user id. In sandbox, "fail" simulates failure.

PaymentLink.description: Razer-style payment-link products only: the full upstream payment URL (e.g. `https://pay.gold.razer.com/order/…`). This — not `uid` — is the target for these products, and the price is flexible (see `confirmed_price_cents`).

additionalProperties.description: Any method-declared required field, forwarded to the upstream.

delivery.description: For products that offer both: `direct` tops up the player account (requires `player.uid`); `voucher` returns a redeem code (no player needed). Defaults to `direct`. Ignored for products that offer only one delivery type.

callback_url.description: Optional per-order webhook URL (in addition to dashboard endpoints).

amount_cents.description: Order cost basis. `0` for BYO / payment-link products (e.g. Razer Payment) — for those the real price is `confirmed_price_cents`, not this field.

fee_cents.description: Topup.dev orchestration fee for this order.

confirmed_price_cents.description: For flexible-priced products (e.g. Razer Payment): the actual price once the engine learns it from the upstream — this, not `amount_cents`, is what the order is worth. `null` at create time and until the price is known.

delivered_code.description: Redeem/voucher code for code-delivery orders (e.g. delivery="voucher"). Null for direct top-ups and until a code is delivered.

batch_id.description: Set when the order was created as part of a bulk batch.

proofs.description: Fulfillment-proof screenshots uploaded by the engine after delivery (e.g. a top-up confirmation). URLs are absolute and unauthenticated (the path UUID is the capability) so you can embed them directly in a customer receipt. Empty until a proof is uploaded.

label.description: Optional display name for the batch (max 120 chars).

items.description: One entry per order. Voucher delivery: `player` may be empty. Direct delivery: each item needs `player.uid` or `player.email`.

status.description: Rolled up from the children. `partial` = some fulfilled, some failed.

RequiredField.description: A player field the upstream needs for this delivery option.

price_cents.description: What you pay Topup.dev per order on this route.

enabled.description: Whether this workspace opted into the service.

ref.description: Deposit txhash / invoice id, if any.

secret_masked.description: Masked secret; full value only on create/rotate.

url.description: https only; public host (no private/internal addresses).

WebhookEvent.description: The body POSTed to your endpoint on each event. Delivered with headers `tg-event` (e.g. `order.fulfilled`) and `tg-signature` (`t=<unix>,v1=<hmac>`). Verify by recomputing `HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<t>.<rawBody>")` and constant-time comparing to `v1`. Endpoints that keep failing are auto-paused (status `errored`).

type.description: Dotted event name. `order.awaiting_confirmation` fires for flexible-priced products (e.g. Razer Payment) when the upstream price needs the shop’s OK — the payload carries `confirmed_price_cents` + `confirmation_expires_at`; act with POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/confirm | /decline before it expires (5-minute window).

amount_cents.description: Cost basis. `0` for BYO / payment-link products — see `confirmed_price_cents`.

confirmed_price_cents.description: Actual price for flexible-priced products (e.g. Razer Payment). Read this — not `amount_cents` — for the order’s real value. `null` for fixed-price products.
